_about: Scientific data library, domain ecology: the universal columns of the game's body/data/ecology.json tables, written by scripts/split_data.py. Same columns/rows schema as the game's tables. `id` is stable (see README); `source` holds source keys from sources.json ('; ' separated) or 'open'. Mark is the review state of these columns. A null in a column the engine's data/*.json holds by the same id means the engine file is the home of that value.

depletion_rules.title: Depletion and regeneration rules
depletion_rules.source: Logistic recovery is the Schaefer model's own; the catch-per-effort fall is the standard signal (CPUE proportional to B); the 'tragedy' row is the Cayman history.
rows: catch = q x effort x B / K (q from Fishing skill, FISHING.md stages); the minigame shows B/K as how many silhouettes appear
B += r B (1 - B/K) / 365 - today's catch (all boats on the ground, aggregate for distant ones)
B under 0.2 K: catch x0.2, the port's fish price up (economy), the fisherman duty yields little
logistic: from 0.2 K back to 0.8 K takes about 2.8/r years (reef fish 7 years, pelagics 3, turtles 56)
live turtles kept in pens do not deplete further but do not breed; a crawl of N feeds N x 30 kg
taking turtles on the beach in nesting season takes breeding females: r x0.5 for that stock for a decade
the same model for game; boucaniers on Hispaniola at MSY x3 drove cattle to near zero by 1700 (history)

soil.title: Soil fertility model
soil.source: A fertility index per field (0 to 1) drained by each crop's demand and restored by manure, fallow and legumes; Barbados exhaustion and the planters' manuring response are the historical anchor (ECO-SOIL). Numbers are placeholders.
rows: f -= demand (cane 0.06, tobacco 0.08, maize 0.03, cassava 0.01, pease -0.02 i.e. restores)
yield = max yield x (0.3 + 0.7 f) x rain factor x labour factor
f += 0.03 per 10 t/ha of dung (cattle pens next to cane fields: the Barbados practice)
f += 0.02 a year idle; +0.04 under bush
clearing forest gives f = 0.9 for a new field but removes firewood for the mill and raises erosion: f -= 0.02 a year extra on slopes
a dry year (under 60% of normal) halves yields; a hurricane destroys standing cane and plantains for a season

nutrient_removal.title: Nutrients removed in the harvested part of a crop
nutrient_removal.source: kg of N, P and K carried off the field per tonne of the harvested part, for the crops of the soil table (CG-20, CG-9). P and K are elemental (P = 0.4364 x P2O5, K = 0.8301 x K2O; an oxide figure is kept in Note). Mark 'researched' = a cited figure changed only in units; 'estimate' = needs a division by a cited yield, or a protein factor, stated in Note. Removal is only the harvested part: tops, trash and leaves left in the field are not counted. Figures are from temperate or global compilations unless Note says tropical; the sources differ by up to a factor of two for K, and none is Caribbean.
rows: Howeler Table 7.1 gives 43 kg N, 20.2 kg P, 96 kg K per ha at 75.2 t/ha fresh cane; divided by the yield. Compilation of tropical literature (Howeler 1991b), locations not stated.
fresh stalks, about 30% dry matter (derived, not stated)

Leite et al. Table 2 mean stalk content 90 kg N, 19 kg P, 266 kg K per ha at 125 t/ha fresh stalk, ratio of means; São Paulo, Brazil, 67 to 211 t/ha. Whole aboveground requirement is higher: 1.4 kg N, 0.24 kg P, 2.7 kg K per t stalk, of which stalks carry about 46% of N, 57% of P, 52% of K.

Howeler Table 7.1: 52 kg N, 6.1 kg P, 105 kg K per ha at 2.5 t/ha dry leaf; divided by the yield. Only one tobacco source was read in full; a Hungarian flue-cured abstract (CORESTA 1991, 35.8 kg N, 6.6 kg P2O5, 57.0 kg K2O per t cured leaf) is cited by a search result but its page returned 403, so it is not entered.
Howeler Table 7.1: 96 kg N, 17.4 kg P, 26 kg K per ha at 6.5 t/ha grain (tropical compilation); divided by the yield.
grain per bushel of 56 lb (25.4 kg); moisture basis of the sheet not read

Culman et al. 2019 (Ohio on-farm trials 2014 to 2018): 0.74 lb N, 0.35 lb P2O5, 0.20 lb K2O per bu = 13.2 kg N, 6.25 kg P2O5, 3.57 kg K2O per t. The sheet notes older tables gave more P and K per bushel.

Howeler Table 7.1: 55 kg N, 13.2 kg P, 112 kg K per ha at 35.7 t/ha fresh roots (high yield). The table's own per-t-dry-matter column does not reconcile with its per-ha column for cassava (4.5/0.83/6.6 printed against 4.1/1.0/8.3 recomputed), so the per-ha figures are used.
fresh roots at a low yield of 15 t/ha

Howeler Fig. 7.2 text: about 30 kg N, 3.5 kg P, 20 kg K per ha at 15 t/ha, 'considerably lower for P and K than previously estimated'; divided by the yield. Spread against the high-yield row: K 2.4 times, P 1.6 times. FAO notes most N and P sit in leaves and stems, so returning them cuts removal.
seed per bushel of 60 lb (27.2 kg); moisture not stated

Manitoba Pulse & Soybean Growers (via Saskatchewan Pulse Growers 2025): at 50 bu/ac, 117 lb N, 34.5 lb P2O5, 35.5 lb K2O per ac = 39.0 kg N, 11.5 kg P2O5, 11.8 kg K2O per t. Per-ha-to-per-t division by the stated yield. Only one pea source was read. Cross-check, not pea: Howeler's common bean row gives 33.6 kg N, 3.3 kg P, 20 kg K per t.
grain, moisture not stated (treated as air-dry)

Susmitha et al. 2022, 598 ICRISAT genebank accessions, India, pooled means: protein 26.99%, P 0.43%, K 1.50%. N = protein / 6.25 = 4.32% (the paper reports protein, not N). Genebank plots, not farm yields; the paper's P unit is inconsistent between tables.

manure_nutrients.title: Nutrients in cattle manure
manure_nutrients.source: kg of N, P and K per tonne of fresh (as-applied) cattle manure with its dry-matter fraction (CG-20, CG-9). Extension tables give lb per short ton as applied; 1 lb/short ton = 0.5 kg/t. P = 0.4364 x P2O5, K = 0.8301 x K2O. Manure varies about 30% with feed, bedding and age; the dry-matter fraction swings the per-tonne figure more than anything else. Mark 'researched' = a cited figure changed only in units.
rows: Beef cattle, open concrete lot, no bedding
fresh solid manure at land application
Purdue AY-277 Table 1: 11 lb N, 7 lb P2O5, 10 lb K2O per ton (4 lb of the N is ammonium). The table's dry-matter cell reads '151' with footnote 1 'open concrete lot': 15% with the marker run on.
Beef cattle, open dirt lot, no bedding
fresh solid manure at land application
Purdue AY-277 Table 1: 21 lb N, 14 lb P2O5, 23 lb K2O per ton; the dry-matter cell reads '522' with footnote 2 'open dirt lot': 52% with the marker run on. Soil in the pen raises dry matter.
fresh solid manure at land application
Purdue AY-277 Table 1: 21 lb N, 18 lb P2O5, 26 lb K2O per ton at 50% dry matter.
fresh solid manure at land application
Purdue AY-277 Table 1: 9 lb N, 4 lb P2O5, 10 lb K2O per ton at 18% dry matter; the bedded dairy row (21% dry matter) has the same figures.
as sold or stored at 76% dry matter; the source does not say fresh or dry basis, read here as the manure at that dry-matter fraction

FAO Table 60 (adapted from Tacon 1987): 1.9% N, 0.6% P, 1.4% K, 34% organic matter. Per dry matter this is about 25 kg N per t dry matter, in line with the fresh rows above (4.5 kg N / 0.18). Aquaculture pond-manure compilation, not a crop source.
Dairy cattle, sun-cured solid manure, two years old
manure at 65% dry matter, N, P, K given as % of dry matter

Velez-Santiago et al. 1985 (Corozal, Puerto Rico): mean over two years and six rates 65% dry matter, 1.6% N, 0.10% P, 0.34% K of dry matter, so per t of manure 650 kg x those fractions. The only Caribbean figure; it is the abstract text as quoted by a search result (the paper's page returned 403), and aged manure has lost N, P and K to weathering.
Loss of N when solid manure is broadcast
fraction of the N lost as ammonia within four days of spreading

Purdue AY-277 Table 4: 15 to 30% of N lost when solid manure is broadcast (0.15 to 0.30); 1 to 5% (0.01 to 0.05) when it is worked in at once. The source gives no storage or open-lot loss fraction, so none is entered.
